Aug 11, 2026

Wagertech <> Jumpr: Weekly Sync

Invited Marc Cabantog lina@wagertech.bet Kobi Kunasekaran emily@wagertech.bet joyce@wagertech.bet Waleed Alasadi Taryn Reithofer Miko Sumagang

Attachments Wagertech <> Jumpr: Weekly Sync

Meeting records Transcript Recording 

Summary

Project status updates and system interface refinements preceded the agreement to pursue a single-system November 1 launch.

Project Status Update
The Alberta expansion launch successfully concluded with ongoing ramping efforts. Data import strategies continue to prioritize current reporting requirements while maintaining consistent operator and partner naming conventions.

System Interface Refinements
User Interface clutter reduction measures involve hiding partner information and legacy deal records to improve visibility. Bonus configurations align with partner-level settings to improve data structure consistency.

System Launch Strategy
The November 1 go-live will utilize a single-system approach to avoid operational complexities. Prediction markets were added to the available vertical categories to expand current platform capabilities.

Decisions

Aligned

  • Migration strategy set to active records The data migration strategy is limited to active deals and operators for the initial phase, deferring historical data to later stages.
  • Inactive deal status added for visibility An 'Inactive' status is added to deals to exclude them from default working views.
  • Salesforce designated owner for operator records Salesforce is designated as the primary owner for creating and managing operator and partner records, which the CMS will ingest.
  • Standardized ID naming convention for records Operator IDs will follow an 'OP-' prefix and Partner IDs will utilize 'PT-' codes to ensure consistent mapping.
  • Rep interface shifted to Assignment page The representative interface is shifted to the Deal Rep Assignment record page, removing the need to navigate to the main deal page.
  • Deposit range field structure updated The deposit range is split into two separate fields (min/max) for configuration, with a formula field added for list views.
  • Global deal naming convention defined The global deal naming convention is set to include the state (or country if multi-state), operator, partner code, and vertical.
  • Bonus fields relocated to Partner record Bonus fields are moved from the Deal level to the Partner record level.
  • Effective End Date removed from view The 'Effective End Date' field is removed from list views to declutter the interface while remaining on the record.
  • Revshare and monthly cap fields added New revenue share and monthly cap fields are added to the deal record configuration.
  • Deal version field removed from records The 'Deal Version' field is removed from the record configuration.
  • System rollout date set The full system rollout is set for November 1st to avoid the complexities of managing parallel systems.
  • Prediction markets vertical added Prediction markets are added as a new option to the list of available verticals.
  • Ad-hoc syncs for feedback The team adopts a new meeting process of booking quick, ad-hoc syncs for incoming feedback to improve project pace.

We've updated the Decisions section using your feedback.

Let us know what you think: Helpful or Not Helpful

Next steps

  • [Kobi Kunasekaran] Enable User Search: Configure permission settings to allow searching for user records.
  • [Joyce Kiddell] Provide Test List: List the deals and brand ambassadors to be used for the initial testing.
  • [Kobi Kunasekaran] Assign Mapping IDs: Update the mapping spreadsheet with proposed operator and partner codes.
  • [Kobi Kunasekaran] Configure Deposit Fields: Create two separate fields for deposit ranges and a conversion formula for quick viewing.
  • [Kobi Kunasekaran] Update Deal Naming: Append the vertical to the default deal name and ensure consistency across the system.
  • [Kobi Kunasekaran] Move Bonus Config: Transfer bonus configuration settings from the deal level to the partner level.
  • [Kobi Kunasekaran] Update Deal Fields: Modify record fields and list view columns for deals and assignments based on the discussed specifications.
  • [Kobi Kunasekaran, Joyce Kiddell] Import Deals: Collaborate to prepare the file for importing deal information into Salesforce.
  • [Joyce Kiddell] Update Documentation: Add prediction markets to the documentation and include it as an option in the vertical list.
  • [Emily Vandenberg] Share Signup Feedback: Submit the collected feedback regarding the signup object through the designated communication channel.
  • [The group] Schedule Meeting: Coordinate and book a follow up session for Thursday or Friday to address operator and partner IDs and outstanding feedback.
  • [Kobi Kunasekaran] Send Utilization Report: Provide the hours utilization report updated through the end of July.

Details

Did the screenshots in this section make your notes better or worse?

  • Alberta Expansion Status: Emily Vandenberg confirmed that the Alberta expansion successfully launched on July 13th. The team is currently navigating a high volume of activity and learning from the initial launch, which remains in a ramping-up phase.
  • Brand Ambassador and User Access: Joyce Kiddell inquired about viewing brand ambassador records in Salesforce. Kobi Kunasekaran clarified that brand ambassadors are classified as "users" rather than "contacts" or "players," and they advised that these records are accessible through standard user profiles. Kobi Kunasekaran noted that players are stored as separate "contacts" or "person accounts," and for ownership logic to function, reps must be registered as Salesforce users (00:01:08) (00:03:52).

  • Survey Completion Testing: Kobi Kunasekaran confirmed that the survey completion test integration conducted by Strad was successful, with no errors reported after previous blocks were removed (00:06:08).

  • ID Mapping Strategy: Kobi Kunasekaran proposed an ID mapping worksheet to facilitate data imports into Salesforce. The team discussed the merits of importing historical data versus only active deals. They reached a consensus to adopt a phased approach: prioritizing the import of active deals to ensure accurate current reporting, with the possibility of backfilling historical data in a later phase .

  • Inactive Deal Management: To prevent UI clutter, the team agreed to implement an "inactive" status for older deals. This will allow the team to hide legacy deals from active working lists without deleting them (00:12:35).

  • Data Requirements for Agency Site Testing: For upcoming agency website testing, Kobi Kunasekaran emphasized the need to import operators, partners, and deals into Salesforce to facilitate mapping. Because the CMS integration is not finalized, the team will create manual ID mappings on the Salesforce side as an interim solution (00:13:26) (00:17:07).

  • CMS and Salesforce Integration Logic: The team discussed the long-term integration between the CMS and Salesforce. Since the CMS lacks a dedicated operator table, they agreed to rely on deal-level information for mapping purposes. Joyce Kiddell confirmed that the team can add new IDs to the database as needed during the testing phase to accommodate new operators or partners .

  • ID Naming Conventions: To ensure consistency and avoid errors during name changes, Kobi Kunasekaran proposed naming conventions for IDs. The team agreed to use a prefix of "OP-" followed by a number for operators and established partner codes (e.g., "PT-") for partners (00:24:36).

  • Deal Console and Representative Access: Kobi Kunasekaran reviewed updates to the Wagertech console, noting that partner information is now hidden from reps to reduce visual clutter. Reps will operate primarily from the "deal rep assignment" page, which provides the necessary data—such as operator, market, and vertical—without requiring them to navigate to the primary deal page (00:28:19).

  • Deposit and Redeposit Range Configuration: Joyce Kiddell requested that deposit ranges be split into separate fields to enable mathematical tracking. Kobi Kunasekaran agreed to implement two configuration fields and a formula field for list views. The team further clarified that redeposit ranges are only necessary if an "immediate" redeposit is selected in the deal configuration (00:31:56) (00:46:51).

  • Deal Naming Conventions: After evaluating different options, the team decided that the global deal name should include the operator, market, vertical, and partner code. Lina Ceniccola confirmed that this streamlined format is acceptable for both operations and rep-facing views, which avoids the need for maintaining duplicate fields or complex list-view structures (00:34:01) (00:39:43).

  • Bonus Configuration Location: Joyce Kiddell noted that bonus configurations should be moved from the deal level to the partner level, as bonuses apply to all deals associated with a specific partner. Kobi Kunasekaran agreed to migrate these fields accordingly (00:42:16).
  • Deal Record Field Cleanup: The team reviewed the edit modal and agreed to remove the "effective end date" from the list view to maintain a cleaner interface. This field will remain on the individual deal record to be populated only when a deal is officially closed (00:46:00).
  • Payout Model and Hybrid Structures: Joyce Kiddell clarified that payout models may involve hybrid structures, such as CPA combined with revenue share. Kobi Kunasekaran agreed to add fields for revenue share percentages that only appear when the hybrid model is selected. Additionally, they agreed to standardize "monthly cap" fields, where a value of zero will indicate unlimited capacity .
  • Removal of Deal Versioning: The team decided to remove the "deal version" field. Kobi Kunasekaran noted that they will rely on the edit log and field history tracking to manage updates rather than using version numbers (00:53:28).
  • Testing Timeline and Rollout Strategy: Emily Vandenberg outlined a phased rollout plan. The team will begin with API testing using low-volume reps next week, followed by high-volume pressure testing. Final UI-based testing will follow, with a full-scale rollout dependent on completing additional features such as redeposit logic, referral management, and two-way sync .
  • System Go-Live Strategy: Kobi Kunasekaran and Emily Vandenberg discussed the transition plan, confirming a goal to go live on November 1. The team decided against a dual-system approach, noting that running parallel systems would be difficult to manage due to the volume of users and the challenges of ensuring representative adoption across multiple markets. Consequently, the team is prioritizing the scoping of all remaining phases in preparation for this launch (00:59:20).
  • Immediate Project Tasks and Testing: Kobi Kunasekaran outlined immediate next steps, which include testing the sign-up logging flow and the agency website. Regarding the Salesforce integration, Kobi Kunasekaran and Joyce Kiddell plan to collaborate on the deal import sheet with the goal of completing testing by the following week. Following this, the team intends to begin discovery and scoping for payouts, redeposits, or the CMS integration, depending on which component becomes ready for development first (01:00:27).
  • Feedback on Operator and Partner Pages: Joyce Kiddell committed to providing feedback on the operator and partner pages, as well as account pages—which include players, referrers, and brand ambassadors—by Thursday (01:00:27).
  • Addition of Prediction Markets: Lina Ceniccola requested the inclusion of "prediction markets" as a new option under the vertical category. Although Kobi Kunasekaran noted that the current vertical options are limited to sports, casino, DFS, and sweepstakes, they agreed to add prediction markets to the list (01:01:39).
  • Agency Website Testing Readiness: Kobi Kunasekaran confirmed that they are ready from a system handling perspective, noting that all flows and automations have been updated. Kobi Kunasekaran stated that as soon as the agency website is ready to be connected, the team will be prepared to begin testing (01:01:39).
  • Meeting Coordination for Reviews: To address feedback on the deals pages, operator/partner IDs, and additional page mockups, Joyce Kiddell and Emily Vandenberg discussed scheduling a follow-up meeting with Kobi Kunasekaran for either Thursday or Friday. Kobi Kunasekaran agreed to the meeting, noting availability on both days, and Emily Vandenberg advised that the team would finalize the booking (01:02:48). Kobi Kunasekaran emphasized that reviewing the mockups during the meeting would be helpful for understanding the proposed changes (01:03:50).
  • Workflow Efficiency: Emily Vandenberg suggested that to improve the pace of the project, the team should book quick syncs as new items arise, rather than waiting, to allow the team to power through the work (01:03:50).
  • Utilization Report Status: Emily Vandenberg requested that Kobi Kunasekaran send over the utilization hours. Kobi Kunasekaran confirmed that the report is updated through the end of July, noting that the previous week's hours were included (01:03:50).
